chunks: As for what Sa'd ibn 'Abd Allah narrated from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from al-Husayn ibn Sa'id and 'Abd al-Rahman ibn Abi Najran and al-'Abbas ibn Ma'ruf, from Hammad ibn 'Isa, from 'Umar ibn Udhaynah, from Zurarah and Bukayr, sons of A'yan, and al-Fudayl ibn Yasar, and Muhammad ibn Muslim, and Burayd ibn Mu'awiya, from Abu Ja'far and Abu 'Abdillah (peace be upon them), that they said:

It is upon the man to give for every person he supports, whether free or slave, young or old. He should give on the day of al-Fitr before the prayer, as that is superior. If he is in ease, he may give it from the first day he enters until the last day of Ramadan. If he gives dates, a sa' for each head; and if he does not give dates, half a sa' of wheat or barley for each head. Wheat and barley are equal: whatever the wheat discharges, the barley discharges.

The aspect in this narration is a form of concession (rukhsah) in advancing the payment of Zakat al-Fitr before its appointed time, as we said regarding the advancement of Zakat al-Mal, although the preference is to discharge it at its proper time, as explicitly stated in the narration.

key_terms.تَقْدِيمُ الزَّكَاةِ: Advancing the payment of charity before its strict deadline
key_terms.حِنْطَةٌ وَشَعِيرٌ: Wheat and barley (primary items for Zakat al-Fitr)
key_terms.رُخْصَةٌ: Concession or leniency in religious law
key_terms.زَكَاةُ الْفِطْرَةِ: Zakat al-Fitr (alms of breaking the fast)
key_terms.صَاعٌ: Sa' (a traditional unit of volume measurement)

ai.seo_question: What are the permissible items and timing for paying Zakat al-Fitr in Shia jurisprudence?
ai.summary: This hadith from al-Isfarayini’s chain in al-Istibsar details the fiqh of Zakat al-Fitr, emphasizing the obligation to cover all dependents and establishing the permissibility of early payment as a concession (rukhsa) while maintaining the superiority of pre-prayer payment. It highlights the equivalence of wheat and barley, reflecting the practical flexibility in Shia jurisprudence regarding the staple food of the region. The text underscores the communal responsibility of the head of household to ensure the spiritual purification of the family before the Eid prayer.
